newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Dell says Compaq plan confusing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dell says Compaq plan confusing.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp chairman Michael Dell said on Tuesday he was more confused than threatened by rival Compaq Computer Corp's move to a build-to-order sales strategy.
Dell said Compaq's plan to sell custom-made computers both through resellers and directly to customers left key questions unanswered, especially about whether it would enable Compaq to lower prices.

"It's not clear what they're going to do...I guess it'll be interesting to see (but) they still have this issue of reseller mark-up," he told Reuters in a phone interview from company headquarters in Round Rock, Texas near Austin.
"The fundamental issue for any company that's not (selling) direct is: how can you justify a mark-up when increasingly customers aren't going to pay for it?," Dell said.

Houston-based Compaq said last month that it would implement a build-to-order system to cut costs, lower prices and better compete with direct sellers like Dell and Gateway 2000. But, unlike them, Compaq will try to implement the strategy partly through retailers, who currently sell 90 percent of Compaq's products.
Whether it will work remains to be seen, Dell said.
"Building to a dealer's order is very different from building to a customer's order," he said.
Dell would not comment on reports that Compaq had tried to buy Gateway to get a solid foothold in the direct-sales marketplace, nor would he say if Compaq had spoken to him about a possible merger.

Dell Computer said on Tuesday that it earned $1.08 a share on revenues of $2.58 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 1998, which ended May 4. That was up from $0.42 a share on revenues of $1.64 billion for the same period a year ago.
Dell would not discuss earnings estimates for the rest of the year or whether the company could maintain such rapid sales growth.

But, he said, "It's a very rapid growth rate for a company of our size. Generally speaking, we wouldn't encourage somebody to think that a company of our size just keeps growing at this rate forever."

The company also said it would do a two-for-one stock split next month, its second stock split in the last eight months. When asked if the board of directors had thought about paying a cash dividend, he said, "We think a 100 percent stock dividend is pretty good."
